answer.short_answer:
In the synthetic randomized trial of 240 adults, the group receiving intervention A had an average HbA1c that was 0.5 percentage points lower than the placebo group after 12 weeks; the 95% confidence interval for this between‑group difference was 0.2 to 0.8 percentage points lower [PubMed:EVAL-NUMBERS].

Because the confidence interval does not include zero, the result is statistically significant, indicating that the observed reduction is unlikely to be due to random variation alone. The estimate applies only to the 12‑week time point, and the trial does not provide data on whether the effect persists beyond that period [PubMed:EVAL-NUMBERS].

The study did not measure mortality or any other clinical outcomes, so no conclusions can be drawn about longer‑term health effects from this data [PubMed:EVAL-NUMBERS].
